_comment: The ROLE GRAPH. A role is a BPMN swimlane — a persona an actor takes on because of the lane it is acting in — and it carries the skills needed to perform that lane's tasks. Actors (who) are in .claude/skills/actors/; skills (what they need to know) are the packages beside this directory. Schema and rationale: schemas/role-graph.ts. `lanes` lists the EXACT lane names this role binds across skills/workflows/*.bpmn. It is a list because the corpus spells one position several ways — sixty distinct lane strings for roughly two dozen positions, measured 2026-09-18 — and declaring the synonyms resolves the existing diagrams without editing twenty BPMN files. A NEW diagram should bind explicitly with <folio:role ref="..."/> on the lane and need not add a name here. `bun run kg:audit` reports any lane no role binds, any role no lane uses, and any activity whose skill its lane's role does not carry.
name: folio-assistant

roles.name: User
roles.summary: The person the assistant is working for. States intent, answers the questions the agent cannot decide from the filesystem, and confirms anything irreversible.

roles.name: Author
roles.summary: Writes and revises folio content. The position, not the person: an editor and a guideline developer both act as author when they are changing a block.

roles.name: Editor
roles.summary: Author plus the authority to accept a change into the corpus. The lane that sees QA findings and decides.

roles.name: Reviewer / SME
roles.summary: Reads a change and judges it. Cannot accept it — that is the editor's lane — and the separation is why review findings are advice rather than commits.

roles.name: QC reviewer
roles.summary: Reviewer with the publication quality gate. Checks the built artefact, not only the source.

roles.name: Clinical / scientific SME
roles.summary: Reviewer whose judgement is about the subject matter rather than the artefact.

roles.name: Programme manager
roles.summary: Owns what gets worked on and holds release authority. The lane that authorises, and the one step no policy may relax.

roles.name: Publication manager
roles.summary: Takes an authorised release to its published form and is accountable for what is live.

roles.name: Business analyst
roles.summary: Turns a stated need into a modelled requirement. Owns the CRDM lane and the BPMN/DMN that come out of it.

roles.name: Terminologist
roles.summary: Owns coded concepts and value sets — the vocabulary a DAK is expressed in.

roles.name: FHIR modeller
roles.summary: Authors the L3 profiles, extensions and examples an IG is built from.
lanes: FHIR modeller / PR author (person + authoring agent)

roles.name: Translation coordinator
roles.summary: Decides what is translated, into which languages, and when a translation is accepted.

roles.name: Human translator
roles.summary: Produces the target-language text. Distinct from the coordinator because accepting one's own translation is the gate this separation removes.

roles.name: Translation adjudicator
roles.summary: Reviewer who settles a disagreement between machine and human translation.

roles.name: Stakeholder
roles.summary: Signs off that a requirement is met. Carries no skills deliberately: sign-off is a judgement, not a procedure, and a skill here would suggest an agent could supply it.

roles.name: Authoring agent
roles.summary: The session agent doing the work. The broadest skill set here, and the one whose membership most needs auditing.

roles.name: Onboarding agent
roles.summary: The authoring agent acting before there is a folio: clarifying what the user means by "create a folio", scanning an existing repo, and scaffolding.

roles.name: Ingestion engine
roles.summary: Runs unattended over a source corpus. No user is in the room, so every gate it reaches must be decidable from the material.

roles.name: Evidence agent
roles.summary: Retrieves and appraises external evidence for a guideline claim.

roles.name: Sibling session
roles.summary: Another agent or human working the same store. Present in bean-lifecycle precisely to mark what is NOT yours to close.
lanes: Sibling session or human (not yours to close)

roles.name: Build pipeline
roles.summary: Validates, renders and publishes. A system lane: it runs a fixed program and exercises no judgement, so anything needing a decision belongs in a different lane.
lanes: Build pipeline — SUSHI · validator · IG Publisher

roles.name: Validation pipeline
roles.summary: The mechanical half of the HCI validation gate. Its findings are inputs to the editor's decision, never the decision.

roles.name: Publish target
roles.summary: GitHub Pages, or wherever the folio is served from. Reached, probed and reported on — never assumed live.

roles.name: Lean toolchain
roles.summary: Elaborates and checks the formal half of a paper folio. Answers only what Lean can answer.

roles.name: IG publisher + validator
roles.summary: The JVM services an IG build shells out to. External in behaviour, internal in configuration.

roles.name: Work plan (beans)
roles.summary: The shared store, modelled as a lane because tasks act ON it and a reader needs to see where the plan is touched. No actor takes this role on; it is acted upon.
lanes: Work plan — beans (shared by humans and agents)

roles.name: Corpus
roles.summary: The versioned content store and the L1 source knowledge graph. Like the work plan, a lane that is written to rather than a participant that acts.

roles.name: External registry
roles.summary: Trusted registries and observatories outside this instance's control. Carries no skills because nothing here instructs it.
